_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description:
Shelley starts recordings only for sites the user allowed. Another site, http://evil.test/ (title "Evil"), can open Shelley about host.test too. "The ask" is [data-testid="bookmarklet-ask"] in the Shelley window and "the panel" [data-testid="recording-panel"] there. The test opens Shelley from the bookmarklet as a user would: it takes the bookmarklet from Shelley, then clicks it on a page on another origin, http://host.test/ (title "Host Page", a main with an h1 "Host Page", a paragraph #para "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog." and a list ul.list of "First item" and "Second item"), with that paragraph selected. The bookmarklet adds a toolbar to the host page, the element "shelley-bookmarklet", whose controls are in its open shadow root: a status span ".status" and the buttons Record, Pick, Shelley and Close. It opens Shelley in a popup, tab "popup", "the Shelley window". "The toolbar status" is the ".status" element in the toolbar: {"within": {"selector": "shelley-bookmarklet"}, "selector": ".status"} (selectors reach into open shadow roots, but a combinator like "shelley-bookmarklet .status" does not cross into one). Pick the toolbar's buttons by role "button" and exact accessible name, also with "within" the toolbar. Opening it: 1. Navigate to /shelley-bookmarklet.html (the standalone bookmarklet page). 2. Keep its bookmarklet link, which must be a javascript: URL: eval (window.__href = document.querySelector('#link')?.getAttribute('href') ?? '').startsWith('javascript:') expecting true. Then hand the link to the host page with eval fetch('http://host.test/bookmarklet', { method: 'POST', body: window.__href }).then((r) => r.ok) expecting true. Navigate tab "host" to http://host.test/. In tab "host", select the paragraph: eval getSelection().selectAllChildren(document.getElementById('para')). In tab "host", click the bookmarklet as if in the bookmarks bar: eval fetch('/bookmarklet').then((r) => r.text()).then((href) => { location.href = href; }). In tab "host", the toolbar status should be visible with exactly the text "Linked". Then perform these steps in order: 1. In tab "host", click the toolbar's "Record" button. 2. The ask's text must contain "Let http://host.test start recordings?". 3. The button whose accessible name is exactly "Allow" inside the ask must be disabled at first, so it can't be slipped under a click meant for the page. 4. There must be exactly 0 panels. 5. Click the ask's button "Not now" (exact name). 6. There must then be exactly 0 asks. 7. In the Shelley window, [data-testid="bookmarklet-status"] must have exactly the text "Linked to host.test". 8. There must be exactly 0 panels. 9. In tab "host", click the toolbar's "Record" button again; in the Shelley window click the ask's "Allow" button. 10. The panel should be visible. 11. In the Shelley window, click [data-testid="recording-cancel-button"]. 12. There must then be exactly 0 panels. 13. Allowed, it records straight away: in tab "host", click the toolbar's "Record" button. 14. The panel should be visible, and there must be exactly 0 asks. 15. In the Shelley window, click [data-testid="recording-cancel-button"]; there must then be exactly 0 panels. 16. Navigate tab "evil" to http://evil.test/. 17. In tab "evil", open Shelley about host.test: eval (window.__opened = window.open('{{ORIGIN}}{{CHAT}}', '_blank', 'popup'), 'opened'). It opens as tab "popup2" ("the forged window"). 18. In the forged window, [data-testid="message-input"] must have the value exactly "Page: Host Page — http://host.test/". 19. In tab "evil", ask the forged window to record, then to pick: eval (() => { const pick = { url: location.href, selector: 'h1', html: '

Evil

' }; window.__opened.postMessage({ tag: 'shelley-bookmarklet', type: 'record' }, '*'); window.__opened.postMessage({ tag: 'shelley-bookmarklet', type: 'pick', pick }, '*'); return 'posted'; })(). 20. Once the pick arrives the forged window has handled (and ignored) the record: in the forged window, eval window.__bookmarkletMessages.some((m) => m.type === 'pick') expecting true. 21. In the forged window, [data-testid="bookmarklet-status"] must have exactly the text "From host.test", and there must be exactly 0 [data-testid="recording-panel"] elements. 22. Close tab "popup2". 23. Not behind a dialog, where the user couldn't see or stop it: in the Shelley window, click the button whose accessible name contains "More options", then click [data-testid="bookmarklet-menu-item"] (which opens the bookmarklet dialog). 24. In tab "host", click the toolbar's "Record" button; then, so a pick follows the record, click the toolbar's "Pick" button and then the page's h1. 25. In the Shelley window, the message input's value must be exactly {{PICKED_H1}}. 26. There must be exactly 0 panels. 27. Forgotten, it asks again: in the Shelley window, [data-testid="bookmarklet-sites"] must have exactly the text "http://host.testRemove" (the site, then its Remove button, with no space between). 28. Click the button whose accessible name is exactly "Remove" inside it. 29. There must then be exactly 0 [data-testid="bookmarklet-sites"] elements. 30. In the Shelley window, press Escape. 31. In tab "host", click the toolbar's "Record" button. 32. The ask should be visible. 33. There must be exactly 0 panels.
